Here's how the two branches relate: one is literally a subset of the other — same commits, not a fork with different changes.

**The short version:** `claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78` and `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` share the exact same commit history, all the way up through the last fake-printer commit. `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` then has three more commits on top that have nothing to do with the fake printer — they're separate UI styling work. So there's no meaningful diff between them on the fake-printer feature itself; it's identical in both.

**The fuller picture, in order:**

1. All three branches you might care about — your current `jusprin-newui`, plus these two — share a common starting point at commit `56eb9a1a46` ("Fail the Windows build script when a step fails"), dated 2026-09-07.

2. From that point, `jusprin-newui` (what you're on now) went off and did unrelated work — things like the MCP tool catalog changes and moving the Agent's OpenAI key into AppConfig. It never got the fake-printer commits.

3. Separately, `claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78` branched off that same point and did the fake-printer work: first a false start (`a162493544`, reverted by `3b14c705a5`), a second false start (`3c244108b4`, reverted by `1408ee3a16`), then the version that stuck — `ecf13456bc` (the Python simulator) and `a25b95fb39` (the C++ side that reports live printer status). That last commit, `a25b95fb39`, is the tip of this branch.

4. `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` contains every single one of those same commits — it's not a copy, it's the identical git history, meaning at some point someone pointed a new branch name at that same commit (or built directly on top of it). Then three more commits were added after it: `a5e5c2fffa` (matching OrcaSlicer's control/container radii), `eff2bdb6af` (defining a token contract for a style sweep), and `0a0e459c6d` (a guard test for radius/spacing/type scales). Those three are about visual design tokens, unrelated to the printer simulator.

**What this means practically:** if you want the fake-printer feature, either branch gives you the same thing. `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` just also carries a small amount of extra, unrelated styling work on top that `claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78` doesn't have. Given the naming pattern (`claude/<description>-<hash>`), the `claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78` branch name looks like it was auto-generated by a Claude Code session working in the background/cloud, and `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` looks like the human-named branch that continued from it.

either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

  entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo owner/name

**Why:** Two separate problems stacked on top of each other:

1. Same issue as before — this repo isn't mirrored on Entire's backend for lookups tied to the server (the `checkpoint explain` command for a commit apparently also needs that link, since even `--search-all` came back "commit not found" for `ecf13456bc` even after I resolved it to its full 40-character hash).

On top of that, this local checkout has its own broken bookkeeping: `entire checkpoint list --json` on your current branch failed with `object not found` while walking a commit's parent chain, even though that exact commit exists fine in git (`git cat-file -t` confirmed it). `entire doctor` (from the last search attempt) also flagged 8 sessions stuck in an "ended with uncondensed checkpoint data" state going back to 2026-09-13/14, which `entire doctor --force` would clean up — that might be related to the parent-chain gap, but I haven't run that since it changes stored session state and you hadn't asked for it.

content.content:
=== full raw commit messages (all trailers) ===
----- a162493544 -----
Add a fake printer agent for testing without hardware

Printer status and print-job code paths previously could not be
exercised at all without a physical printer connected: every
IPrinterAgent implementation in the tree talks to real hardware or a
real network endpoint, and no test covered any of them.

FakePrinterAgent is an IPrinterAgent implementation backed by a scripted
status sequence instead of a real MQTT/LAN connection. It replays a
canned "connect -> heat -> print -> finish" timeline, pushing the same
Bambu-style push_status JSON a real printer sends through the same
callbacks, so code downstream of the interface cannot tell the
difference.

It can be driven two ways:

- Automated, from test code: connect_printer(), start_local_print() and
  push_status() are called directly. Three Catch2 cases cover full
  scenario replay, single-status injection, and cancellation.
- Manually, by a person: setting JUSPRIN_FAKE_PRINTER_CONSOLE=1 starts a
  numbered menu on stdin for connecting, replaying the scenario, and
  jumping to named presets (Idle, Heating, Printing 25%/75%, Finished,
  Failed). Nothing to memorize and no parameters to type.

Registration follows the existing pattern exactly: one register_agent<T>
line, the same way every other printer agent is discovered. The registry
is bootstrapped by an explicit list rather than self-registering statics,
so a new implementation still needs that line. Total footprint outside
the two new files is four lines.

Scope limit worth knowing: this exercises the IPrinterAgent layer only.
It does not touch MoonrakerPrinterAgent or the PrintHost family, which
speak real wire protocols and remain untested. It also has no visible
effect in the JusPrin shell today, which hides the sidebar and tab strip
and contains no reference to MachineObject, so no screen in this branch
renders the resulting status for a non-Bambu printer.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M1Y935HXX2F3ZX7PMSTEP2XQ


----- 3c244108b4 -----
Let the fake printer drive the header printer chip

The chip's connection line (Not connected / Offline / Idle / Printing) is
the only field in the printer and spool menus that comes from a printer
rather than from presets, and it reported state for Bambu printers only.
That left the fake printer agent with nothing to drive, and no way to
switch it on either: the Physical Printer dialog is the only UI exposing
the printer_agent and print_host fields it needs, and this shell hides
the sidebar that opens it.

Three changes:

- The chip also reports live state when the active printer agent is the
  simulator. Gated on the agent rather than on "not Bambu", so every real
  printer keeps its current behaviour, including the deliberate "not
  connected" shown for other print hosts.
- Setting JUSPRIN_FAKE_PRINTER installs the simulator and registers and
  selects a synthetic LAN device, so no dialog is needed. The same
  variable now starts the manual console, which previously had its own.
- switch_printer_agent() leaves the simulator installed while that
  variable is set. Without this it replaced the agent roughly 400ms after
  startup and cleared its callbacks, so pushed status vanished silently.

Verified against the running app. With the variable set, the selected
device stays FAKE001 and both the automatic connect and a status pushed
from the console reach MachineObject::parse_json, which is what feeds the
chip. With it unset, no device is registered, no console starts, and the
agent switches to orca exactly as before.

Upstream footprint for the whole feature is ten lines: two registering
the agent, two in CMakeLists, and six guarding switch_printer_agent.
Everything else lives in fork-owned files.

Not covered: the chip's own rendering, which needs a screen session.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M1ZE7S9K34E1NR5XA49CCXMY


----- 1408ee3a16 -----
Revert "Let the fake printer drive the header printer chip"

This reverts commit 3c244108b495c7918f76f45360d9a1f55b87c7f1.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M1ZQ7TGKQTJ30Q7YYZ6X4RD3


----- 3b14c705a5 -----
Revert "Add a fake printer agent for testing without hardware"

This reverts commit a1624935446208e009334270b5a237976cb9f6d6.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M1ZQ7WJAAXR17T2VVWXR6YVC


----- ecf13456bc -----
Add a fake Moonraker printer for testing without hardware

Nothing in the tree could exercise sending a print or reading printer
status without a physical printer. Two earlier attempts built a fake
IPrinterAgent inside the app; both were reverted because they bypassed
every line of real network code and needed upstream registration.

tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py is a stand-alone Moonraker (Klipper)
printer in plain Python, standard library only. JusPrin reaches it through
its real Moonraker code: the Print button's server check, upload and
print-start requests, and the printer agent's connect, status query and
websocket stream (identify, subscribe, notify_status_update). A started
print heats up and progresses on its own; a small G-code interpreter
handles the commands the agent sends. A /sim control API sets the
printer's state (printing, paused, offline, temperatures, Klipper down)
and returns a log of every request the app made, which is what a person
or an AI agent asserts on.

JusPrin's shell hides the dialog that sets a print host, so
--install-preset writes a user printer preset pointing at the simulator
(printer_model "Fake Moonraker", so the header chip names it) and selects
it in the app config. It copies the vendor's version string because a
preset whose version does not parse is silently skipped at load.

mac_post_key.swift posts key events to the app's process so an agent can
slice and press Print without a screen; this also works while the Mac is
locked, where screenshot tools are refused.

23 unit tests drive the simulator with the exact request shapes from
Moonraker.cpp and MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp. Verified against the built
app twice: it uploaded the sliced cube and started the print, and the
simulator ran it to completion. The README carries the manual and the
agent procedures, and engineering-method.md points at it.

Known limits: opening a saved 3mf switches to the printer stored in it;
the agent dials https while enable_ssl_for_mqtt is true (a separate fix);
no authentication and no Happy Hare mmu object.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M20Q1FN6CP7PQP3VJJ7FHG4J


----- a25b95fb39 -----
Report a print host's live state in the printer menu

The printer menu's first row said "Not connected" for every non-Bambu
printer: SetupCommands::printer_connection returned early unless the
preset used the Bambu network, and the Moonraker agent never received
status after its first hello because upstream compiled out the status
query and websocket stream (their Device tab shows a Klipper printer's
own web page instead, so their native panel never needed the data).
JusPrin hides that tab and wants a state word, so both had to change.

SetupCommands::printer_connection now reports the selected machine's
state for any preset with a print host, provided the machine's dev_id
matches that host; a preset without a host, such as one restored from a
saved 3mf, stays "Not connected" even though the previous machine is
still selected in the device manager. monitor_available is true only for
Bambu, since Orca's monitor tab knows nothing else, and the menu row
stays enabled without the monitor icon when there is a state to show.

MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp: the upstream "#if 0" around the initial status
query and start_status_stream becomes "#if 1", with a comment naming the
consumer. That is the only upstream-owned change (+3/-1); no upstream
line was deleted or rewritten, and the fork owns a policy (print hosts
report live state), not upstream behaviour. Rebase evidence: upstream/main
(1170b048e8) still carries the identical disabled block, and
git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=8500fcdcca upstream/main <tree>
reports no conflict in any file this commit touches (the fork's four
existing conflicts are elsewhere). Should upstream enable the block
themselves, the resolution is to take their side and drop the comment.

Verified on the rebuilt app against tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py
with screenshots of the menu: Idle with the simulator up, Printing after
sending a print from the app, Offline about 30 seconds after the
simulator stopped answering, and a fresh websocket subscription once it
came back. Bambu printers take the same path as before. The agent still
dials https while enable_ssl_for_mqtt is true; that fix is separate.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M20Q1HAW20CHTR3Z4RAG3H0R

**Verified fact:** the commit chain that produced these six commits sits entirely inside a branch called `claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78`. The reflog for that branch shows it was created directly off `jusprin-newui` right after the two reverts, then had the two final commits (`ecf13456bc`, `a25b95fb39`) added, then got rebased onto a later point in the branch:

```
claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78@{3}: branch: Created from refs/heads/jusprin-newui

claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78@{0}: rebase (finish): ... onto f60ec4be63
```

**My hypothesis, based on comparing branch-naming patterns already in this repo:** this points to Claude Code, not Codex. Here's why. This repository has dozens of branches from both tools, and they follow visibly different naming conventions:

- Every `claude/...` branch follows `claude/<description-in-kebab-case>-<6-character-hex-suffix>` — for example `claude/agent-webview-bridge-phase-1-16c7bb`, `claude/add-printer-flow-page-b26bf5`, or (when no clear description exists) an adjective-plus-scientist-name codename like `claude/peaceful-kalam-70d5e4` or `claude/modest-wozniak-ec599e`.

`claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78` matches the first pattern exactly (description + 6-hex suffix), and doesn't match the Codex pattern at all. That's a strong signal, but it's an inference from a naming convention, not a direct confirmation — I'd call it "very likely Claude Code" rather than certain, since I can't independently verify it through Entire's session records the way I could if that lookup were working.

One more data point in the same direction: the commit messages themselves (long, structured prose with sections like "Scope limit worth knowing," explicit verification steps, and — in `a25b95fb39` — a rebase-safety citation against `upstream/main` with a `git merge-tree` conflict check) match the writing style this project's `AGENTS.md` explicitly asks agents to follow for changes to upstream-owned files. # Fake Bambu printer — what landed, why, commits, how to use

This is an **in-process stand-in for Bambu’s closed network plugin**. It is not a fake printer on the wire (no MQTT, FTPS, or discovery). With a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected, JusPrin’s Bambu UI paths — printer-menu Idle / Printing / Offline, Select Machine, and Send print job — run without hardware.

The operator guide in the tree is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

---

## Why

Two earlier attempts were reverted because they looked like a fake printer but never entered the Bambu UI:

| Commit | What it did | Why it failed |
|---|---|---|
| `a162493544` | `FakePrinterAgent` under its **own** agent id, plus a non-Bambu preset | Every Bambu-only gate (`is_bbl_vendor()`, Select Machine, print job) rejected it |
| `3c244108b4` | Special-cased the header chip so the fake could show Idle / Printing / Offline | Patched a symptom. Kenneth reverted both because nothing visible worked |

A separate Moonraker/Klipper simulator already exists on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` (`tests/printer_sim/`). That fakes the **print-host** HTTP/websocket path. Bambu is a different agent (`"bbl"` wrapping `libbambu_networking`). Faking Bambu’s network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and rejected.

Kenneth’s decisions for this work: emulate **A1 mini (`N1`)**, control surface is a **JSON file only** (no MCP tools), keep the Moonraker simulator for Klipper.

---

## Design that actually works

Keep a **real Bambu system preset** selected so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true. Then substitute the fake **only at the printer-agent factory**, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`.

The one upstream seam is three additive lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp`). No upstream line was deleted or rewritten:

```3574:3579:src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp
    if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor()) {
        effective_agent_id = BBL_PRINTER_AGENT_ID;
        cloud_agent_id = BBL_CLOUD_PROVIDER;
        // Fork policy: fake mode substitutes the Bambu agent. Additive; no upstream line deleted.
        if (const std::string fake_id = fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config); !fake_id.empty())
            effective_agent_id = fake_id;
```

If `is_bbl_vendor()` is false, this branch never runs and the agent stays `orca` or `moonraker`. That is why an embedded 3mf preset named “Bambu Lab A1 mini …” is not enough: BBL vendor files must be installed under `<datadir>/system/`.

The fake implements `IPrinterAgent`. It announces device `FAKE001` via the same SSDP-style JSON the Moonraker agent uses, then `DeviceManager` creates a `MachineObject`. Status is a Bambu `push_status` heartbeat about once a second. Offline is “stop pushing”; after ~30 s (`DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT`) the menu first row is Offline.

Heartbeat does **not** start in the constructor. Tests that never call `set_queue_on_main_fn` stay quiet. The GUI always sets that callback last, which is when the heartbeat starts.

---

## What shipped

Fork-owned agent:

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.hpp`
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp`
- Wired in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake`

Behavior:

- Registers as `jusprin-fake-bambu` via `NetworkAgentFactory::register_printer_agent`
- Reads `jusprin.fake_printer` from AppConfig (JSON boolean stored as the string `"true"`)
- Control file: `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json`, reread ~1s
- Printer type `N1`; Select Machine lists **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**
- `start_local_print` logs the filename. With no control file it replays a canned idle→print scenario. With a control file, send still succeeds and the file’s state wins
- After SSDP, queues access codes then `MonitorPanel::select_machine` / `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine` on the main thread

Tests: `tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`, target `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (GUI build). Announce JSON, control-file parsing, agent id, canned scenario. They do not start the heartbeat unless the test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

Docs pointers: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `engineering-method.md`, `orca-integration-guide.md` §4.

The planning handoff `agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md` was never committed and was deleted after the work landed. It was stale (“not started”) and contradicted the operator README.

E2E on 2026-09-08 (scratch `FakeBambuTest.app`, isolated datadir): log showed `jusprin-fake-bambu` and `set_selected_machine=FAKE001`; menu Idle → Printing via control file → Offline after `"offline":true`; Cmd+R slice; Cmd+Shift+G send listed the fake LAN machine and completed with `start_local_print` in the log.

---

## Commits

Authored on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7`, then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (one CMake conflict: keep both `shell_theme_tests` and `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests`). Both cherry-picks are on `origin/jusprin-newui`.

| Role | Worktree SHA | `jusprin-newui` SHA | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| Implementation | `72df8f3678` | `7acf075aaa` | Substitute an in-process fake for the Bambu printer agent when testing without hardware |
| Operator docs | `ca7e517000` | `e04c0d40d3` | Document how to operate the fake Bambu printer for humans and agents |

`7acf075aaa` is the one to cite on the production branch. Bodies:

- Implementation: keep a real Bambu preset selected and swap the closed plugin for `FakeBambuAgent` so header menu, Select Machine, and print job can run without a printer. (~1253 lines: agent, 4-line `GUI_App` seam, initial README, Catch2 tests, engineering-method pointer.)
- Docs: the first README used INI config and treated the chip as the status surface. The follow-up records JSON config, a real Bambu **system** preset, isolated-instance rules, and the printer-menu first row.

Cherry-pick parent of `7acf075aaa` is `367f5703b3` (then-tip of `jusprin-newui`). The worktree commits sat on `a9adaae973` (token-scale guards), which is why they were cherry-picked rather than merged.

---

## How to use it

Canonical steps: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

### 1. Isolated datadir

Quit JusPrin. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit. Use a **scratch** `--datadir`, not the everyday config.

If another JusPrin is already running, set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

### 2. Turn the fake on

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored. AppConfig maps JSON booleans to the string `"true"`.

### 3. Real Bambu **system** preset

Select `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle` (or another BBL system machine). `is_bbl_vendor()` must be true.

Install via **Add a printer…**, or copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into `<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini to the `models` array. Opening `Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps **after** that vendor is installed.

### 4. Confirm it switched

In `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log` (use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on this machine; default `grep` may be ugrep):

- `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- `set_selected_machine=FAKE001`
- later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is **not** in the path. Fix the preset. Do not patch UI gates.

The chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle). Idle / Printing / Offline are the **first row of the printer menu**, opened by clicking the printer half of the chip (`SetName("Printer")`). Those words are never on the chip.

### 5. Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). Reread ~once a second:

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1 → `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

### 6. Print

Slice, then Print (Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Select Machine lists **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**. Send completes without a printer. Log: `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, send still succeeds but the menu stays on the file’s state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing walk after send.

### 7. Agents: do not drive the wrong app

Another JusPrin may already be open. On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto’d `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`). Do not `pkill` by name.

Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer chip often has no AX title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use Print’s shortcut. Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events posted that way do not.

### 8. Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` in a GUI build.

---

What this does **not** cover: Moonraker/Klipper (other branch), a fake Bambu network stack, or MCP tools to set state. Those were out of scope on purpose.

---
name: fake-bambu-printer-sim
description: "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.{hpp,cpp} — the in-process Bambu printer stand-in that IS on jusprin-newui (unlike the Moonraker simulator); keeps a real Bambu system preset selected and substitutes only the agent."
metadata:
  type: project
---

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

Doc pointers added in the two landing commits: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` ("Printer tests without hardware" section), `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`. A planning handoff doc (`agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md`) was never committed and doesn't exist in the tree — don't look for it.

**Why:** Kenneth wants Bambu-path testing (header menu state, Select Machine, print job) without hardware, on the branch he actually works on day to day — distinct from the Moonraker/Klipper simulator, which stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` and covers the print-host HTTP path instead.

**How to apply:** For "fake a printer on jusprin-newui" requests, this is the one that's actually there — check `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/` first. See [[verify-current-branch-before-memory-recall]] for why this file exists: an earlier session answered "how do we fake a printer" from the Moonraker memory alone and missed this entirely, because it never grepped the current tree for "fake"/"Testing" before recalling.

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **real Bambu Lab system preset** selected, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`. `is_bbl_vendor()` must be true. An embedded
3mf preset named `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough;
the agent stays `orca`.

Install the system preset with **Add a printer…** in the printer menu, or copy
`Resources/profiles/BBL` into `<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to
the `models` array in `JusPrin2.conf`. Opening `~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf`
only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

## Agent id

Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_ax_find
entries.description:
Search the accessibility elements captured by the last app_screenshot of one window. Filter by role (e.g. "AXTextArea", "AXButton") and/or title substring. Returns matching elements with their [N] index — pass that as element_index to app_click/app_type. Use this when the inline summary in app_screenshot doesn't show the element you need (it only lists the first few actionable ones).

This tool acts on one application in the BACKGROUND while the user keeps working in other apps. The target window does not come to the front. For the menu bar use app_menu; hover states, context menus, and canvas-style drags still need the display-scope screenshot/left_click tools (which do take over the screen).

app.description: Bundle identifier of the target application (e.g. "com.apple.TextEdit"). Must be in the granted-applications list — call request_access first if it isn't.

window_id.description: CGWindowID from app_list_windows or from a previous app_screenshot result. If omitted, defaults to the window you most recently app_screenshot-ed for this app (or the app's main window if you haven't screenshotted yet). Pass a different id to switch windows — there is no separate switch-window tool; targeting is per-call via this parameter.

role.description: Exact AX role to match (e.g. "AXButton", "AXTextArea", "AXLink", "AXComboBox"). Omit to match any role.

title_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against the element's title. Omit to match any title.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_batch
entries.description:
Execute a sequence of app_* actions against ONE window in a single tool call. Each individual app_* call is a model→API round trip; batching a predictable sequence (e.g. click a field, type into it, press return) eliminates all but one. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error or 'unsupported' result. An 'ineffective' result (write accepted, app didn't visibly respond yet) does NOT stop the batch — include a screenshot action after to verify. Include {"action":"screenshot"} anywhere in the list to capture the window at that point — coordinates and element_index in actions AFTER a screenshot refer to that screenshot. Put one last to see the post-batch state in the same call.

content.text:
## Test results: the fake Bambu printer works as documented, and it's genuinely off by default

I ran two isolated test instances of the built app (separate bundle id, scratch data directories, never touching your live JusPrin session), following the README step by step.

**Disabled by default — confirmed.** With `jusprin.fake_printer` left unset and a real Bambu Lab A1 mini preset selected, the log shows `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to bbl` — the real agent, no trace of `jusprin-fake-bambu` anywhere. So the feature is inert unless someone explicitly opts in.

**Enabled — every documented claim checked out:**
- Log showed all three lines the README promises: `switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`, `set_selected_machine=FAKE001`, `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`.
- Header chip read exactly `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4`, as documented.
- Clicking the printer chip's menu showed **Idle** as the first row.
- Writing `{"state":"printing",...}` to the control file flipped the menu to **Printing** within ~1 second.
- Writing `{"offline":true}` produced **Offline** after about 36 seconds — matching the doc's "~30 s" claim closely.
- Sliced the test cube, hit Print, and the send dialog correctly listed the printer as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini(LAN)**. Sending it logged `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...3mf`, confirming a full send completes with no real printer.

**One thing I noticed that the doc doesn't cover:** after that successful send, the printer menu started reading "Not connected · Prints go to a card" instead of going back to Idle, even though the fake agent's own status pushes kept flowing normally in the log (still `dev_id=FAKE001`, `gcode_state: IDLE`). This wasn't a documented behavior one way or the other, so I can't call it a bug outright — it could be an existing quirk in how the printer-menu status is computed after a print job is sent, unrelated to the fake agent itself, since the agent-side connection never actually dropped. I didn't chase it further since it's outside what you asked me to verify. Let me know if you'd like me to dig into that specifically.

with an isolated scratch --datadir:
1. Enabled fake mode, selected "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle" system preset, launched
   with tests/data/20mm_cube.obj.

   row correctly showed Idle, then Printing (after writing
   {"state":"printing",...} to <datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json), then Offline
   (~36s after {"offline":true}) — all matching the README.
3. Sliced the cube, clicked Print, the send dialog correctly listed
   "JusPrin Fake A1 mini(LAN)", clicked Send. The debug log confirmed success:
   `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...3mf dest=`.
4. AFTER that successful send, I reopened the printer-menu (click the printer half
   of the header chip) and it now showed "Not connected" / "Prints go to a card."
   instead of returning to Idle — even though the FakeBambuAgent kept pushing valid
   status in the log the whole time (dev_id=FAKE001, gcode_state=IDLE, no
   disconnect). This never recovered on its own; reopening the menu repeatedly still
   showed "Not connected."

(`status_word = "Not connected"`, `sub_label = "Prints go to a card."`), which is
presumably driven by src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.cpp's
